rubric.why: Identifies that two pairs of electrons are involved.
rubric.description: States that two pairs of electrons are shared.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying two shared electron pairs.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a double covalent bond from other bonds.
rubric.description: States that the sharing occurs between two atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the atoms involved in the covalent sharing.

modelAnswer: A double covalent bond is formed when two atoms share two pairs of electrons.
The shared pairs hold the two atoms together.

items.followUp: What is meant by a covalent bond?

rubric.why: Identifies hydrogen and the electronegative atom involved in hydrogen bonding.
rubric.description: Mentions hydrogen associated with a highly electronegative atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying hydrogen and an appropriate electronegative atom.

rubric.why: Describes the attractive nature of the bond.
rubric.description: Identifies hydrogen bonding as a weak attraction, usually between molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a weak attractive force.

modelAnswer: A hydrogen bond is a weak force of attraction between a hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom and another electronegative atom.
It usually occurs between neighbouring molecules.

items.followUp: Name four types of chemical bonds.

rubric.why: Names a principal type of chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming ionic or electrovalent bonding.

rubric.why: Names another type of chemical bond.
rubric.description: Names at least one other type of chemical bond.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a type other than ionic bonding.

modelAnswer: The types of chemical bonds include ionic (electrovalent), covalent, coordinate covalent and metallic bonds.
Hydrogen bonding is also described as a type of chemical bond.

items.followUp: How do intermolecular forces affect the vapour pressure of a liquid?

rubric.why: Connects stronger attractions between particles with lower vapour pressure.
rubric.description: States that stronger intermolecular forces result in lower vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship between strong forces and low vapour pressure.

rubric.why: Explains the behaviour of more volatile liquids or liquids with weaker attractions.
rubric.description: States that volatile liquids, or liquids with weaker intermolecular forces, have higher vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship between volatility or weaker forces and higher vapour pressure.

modelAnswer: Liquids with strong intermolecular forces have low vapour pressure because fewer particles escape from the liquid surface.
Volatile liquids, with weaker intermolecular forces, have higher vapour pressure.

items.followUp: Define reduction in terms of electrons.

rubric.why: Gives the defining electron change for oxidation.
rubric.description: States that oxidation is the loss of electrons.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct definition.

modelAnswer: Oxidation is the loss of one or more electrons by an atom, ion or molecule.

items.followUp: State two chemical characteristics of metals.

rubric.why: Provides one valid physical characteristic of metals.
rubric.description: States one physical characteristic of metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct physical characteristic.

rubric.why: Provides a second valid physical characteristic.
rubric.description: States a second physical characteristic of metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct characteristic.

modelAnswer: Metals are malleable and can be beaten into sheets.

rubric.why: Gives one valid use of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one correct use.

rubric.why: Gives a second valid use of silver.
rubric.description: States a second use of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct correct use.

modelAnswer: Silver is used for making ornaments and jewellery.
It is also used in photographic films and for silvering mirrors.

items.followUp: Explain any three branches of Chemistry.

rubric.why: Explains two branches of Chemistry with their subject matter.
rubric.description: Defines physical chemistry and organic chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each correct branch and its area of study.

rubric.why: Identifies the study of chemical processes in living systems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it studies chemical substances or processes in living organisms.

rubric.why: Identifies the application of chemistry in industry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it deals with manufacturing chemicals or chemical products.

rubric.why: Gives an explanation of an additional branch of Chemistry.
rubric.description: Explains one other branch, such as nuclear, environmental, analytical or inorganic chemistry.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the subject matter of any one additional branch.

modelAnswer: Physical chemistry studies the physical properties of matter and the changes in energy accompanying chemical reactions.
Organic chemistry is the branch that studies carbon compounds.
Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and processes in living organisms.
Industrial chemistry deals with the manufacture of chemicals and other products on an industrial scale.
Nuclear chemistry studies changes in the nuclei of atoms, including radioactive processes.
